facts.text: Cullman was founded in 1873 by Colonel John G. Cullmann, a German immigrant who negotiated land for a colony of German settlers.
The town’s name was Americanized to “Cullman” with one “n” when it incorporated in 1874.
Cullman is known for its German roots, walkable downtown, lively festivals, scenic lakes, and small‑town warmth.
The Cullman County Museum, located in downtown, showcases local history with exhibits on a former governor, military relics, and vintage children’s toys.
Cullman’s public television station, CCTV55, is run by students at Cullman High School, giving the town a unique media presence.
Cullman sits along Interstate 65, about 50 miles north of Birmingham and 55 miles south of Huntsville, placing it between two major Alabama cities.
